claims.text: The identity of X governs the long-term stability of the protective oxide scale in CrFeCoNiX alloys through its oxygen affinity and oxidation kinetics.
Si has sufficiently high oxygen affinity to undergo preferential oxidation in CrFeCoNiSi.
Preferential oxidation of Si produces an amorphous, SiO2-rich surface layer.
The SiO2-rich layer is chemically inert and slow-growing.
The SiO2-rich layer can incorporate chromium-oxide species.
Incorporation of chromium oxides into the SiO2-rich layer relieves interfacial stress.
An amorphous, glassy oxide accommodates lattice mismatch and reduces internal stress.
The SiO2-rich layer inhibits rapid oxidation kinetics.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form comparatively polycrystalline oxide scales.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form comparatively polycrystalline oxide scales.
The Mn- or Al-derived polycrystalline scales develop higher intrinsic growth stresses than the proposed Si-rich scale.
Higher oxide growth stresses promote cracking and spallation.
Under identical oxidation conditions, Si-containing alloys will form thinner, more uniform, and more adherent scales with slower growth and less cracking than Mn- or Al-containing alloys.
CrFeCoNi without an X addition can serve as a control for isolating the effect of Si.
The proposed comparison applies to single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys.
The proposed test uses isothermal oxidation above 900 °C, exemplified by approximately 950 °C in controlled air.
The hypothesis may not extrapolate to lower temperatures or non-oxidative corrosive conditions.
